## Overview

Dune: Imperium – Uprising is a deck-building worker placement game set in the Dune universe. Each player is a Leader representing one of the Great Houses of the Landsraad (or another powerful figure). You play cards to send Agents to board spaces, acquire new cards for your deck, deploy units (troops and sandworms) to the Conflict, and grow Influence with the four Factions (Emperor, Spacing Guild, Bene Gesserit, Fremen). At the end of a round, if any player has reached **10 or more Victory Points** (or the Conflict Deck is empty), the game ends and whoever has the most VP wins.

Compared with base Dune: Imperium, the rulebook's difference notes call out: Spies and observation posts, a new **Spy** Agent icon, additional board spaces requiring 2 Influence with a Faction, sandworms and Maker Hooks, Battle Icons and Sandworm Reward Doubling, Objective cards (which determine the first player), and the new optional CHOAM Module. There is **no Mentat** Agent and there are **no Foldspace** cards. Cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.

**Scope:** Original English 2023 Uprising, rulebook version 23-10-12: complete standard 2–4-player play, including the required two-player Rival rules below, plus the optional standard base-box CHOAM Module. Solo-only rules, all optional Rival variants (including Streamlined Rivals), six-player teams and cross-game expansions are excluded. In two-player play use an ordinary scoring Rival, rather than the two Streamlined-only Rivals Lady Amber Metulli and Glossu “The Beast” Rabban. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts are identified for sorting only and are not used in this scope. Board-space rules come from the publisher’s Uprising Board Space Guide; the labeled FAQ section uses relevant clarifications from the official January 13, 2025 FAQ.

At **4 Influence**, there are **two separate rewards with different reversal rules**: (a) gain the printed **track bonus**, keep it if you fall below 4, and earn it again on returning to 4; (b) the **first player to 4 gains the Alliance token and 1 VP**, but that VP remains tied to holding the token. **When a challenger gains Influence, tying the current holder does not steal the Alliance; rising above the holder transfers the token and its 1 VP.** An Alliance is therefore a temporary VP, unlike the retained track bonus. **Official FAQ — a separate transfer trigger is the holder losing Influence:** if previously tied, the formerly tied opponent takes the token; if several were tied, the former holder chooses its recipient. ## Special Rules & Edge Cases

- **Spies & observation posts:** Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional: you may decline even if a legal placement or recall exists. Declining a recall used as a cost also declines its associated benefit; an Intrigue still requires paying all its costs to play it. Observation posts around the board each connect to one or more board spaces. The **Spy icon** (on a card or board space) lets you place a Spy from your supply on an **unoccupied** observation post; if you have no Spies in your supply when you need to place one, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. Some placement effects (e.g., from the Lady Margot Fenring Leader) specify a particular Agent icon that must be connected to the post — otherwise you can't place the Spy. The **Recall Spy icon** on a card returns one of your Spies from a post to your supply (usually as a cost for a powerful effect). A Spy may also be recalled **without a card** for one of two effects: **Infiltrate** — if you wish to send an Agent to a board space occupied by another player, recall your own Spy from a connected post to ignore the other player's Agent and send your Agent to that same space; **Gather Intelligence** — whenever you send an Agent to a board space, you may recall your own Spy from a connected post to draw a card, deciding immediately after placing your Agent (before receiving any effects of the space or the card you played). Infiltrate cannot bypass your own Agent: it only bypasses another player’s Agent. You cannot recall the same Spy to both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence (though on certain spaces, like the Research Station, you may recall one Spy to Infiltrate and another Spy to Gather Intelligence). The **Spy Agent icon** on a card lets you send an Agent to any board space connected to an observation post where you currently have a Spy — you do **not** recall the Spy for this.
